svg.text: Encrypted ExpressRoute: IPsec over ExpressRoute with Routing Intent
Two-pass Secured Hub inspection path, BGP prefix specificity rules, and throughput guardrails (SEC-08 / FAQ 8)
Forwards outer ESP over ER Private
Disjoint or longer mask on VPN BGP!
If identical prefixes are advertised on
both ER and VPN, Azure prefers the
IDPS Bypass List on tunnel IPs!
Why Single-Tunnel Throughput Caps Near ~1 Gbps
Routing Intent steers outer ESP packets through Hub Firewall before VPN Gateway
decryption, then steers decrypted inner packets through Hub Firewall again.
Scale >1 Gbps via Azure Firewall Premium + GCMAES256 + ECMP multi-tunnels.
Transport Encryption Trade-Off: IPsec over ExpressRoute vs. ExpressRoute Direct MACsec
Option A: IPsec VPN over ExpressRoute (Provider or Direct Circuits)
Encrypts end-to-end between on-premises VPN headend and Hub S2S VPN Gateway.
Subject to ~1 Gbps per-tunnel ceiling under Routing Intent; scale via ECMP tunnels.
Option B: ExpressRoute Direct with MACsec (10 Gbps / 100 Gbps Line Rate)
IEEE 802.1AE GcmAes256 Layer-2 encryption between customer edge and MSEE.
Zero IPsec encapsulation overhead or Hub Firewall outer-ESP pass; requires ER Direct.
